edition.title: The Daily Signal
edition.kicker: Primary-source tech intelligence, compiled from the live wire.

stories.title: GPT-6 Astra goes broadly available: ChatGPT, API, and Microsoft Foundry in one day
stories.summary: OpenAI moved GPT-6 Astra from a Daybreak-limited launch to broad availability across ChatGPT Work/Codex, the API, and Microsoft Foundry for all Azure customers, with CEO Sam Altman saying Plus and Business access is live despite the launch post allowing 'a few days.' API pricing is $10/$50 per million input/output tokens (2x at >272K context), and Azure mirrors short-context pricing at $20/$75 for long-context Global. This is the day a Critical-rated cyber model stopped being a preview: the practical question shifts to reliability at scale, with fine-tuning and audio/video I/O still unsupported.

quality.note: Official OpenAI launch page plus three in-window official posts (OpenAI, OpenAIDevs, sama). Availability rollout details differ slightly between posts; capability claims remain OpenAI-reported.

stories.title: Anthropic's Claude agents produced the first end-to-end machine-checked Lean 4 proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
stories.summary: Anthropic published a complete, kernel-checked Lean 4 formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem (the Frey-Serre-Ribet-Wiles-Taylor route) built in about 11 days by a Claude Code / Prove2Me multi-agent harness, writing ~13M lines of Lean and proving ~30,300 theorems. The build rests on exactly Lean's three standard axioms, was confirmed by the Lean comparator against Mathlib's own statement, and was accepted by an independent Rust kernel (nanoda); the repo ships a browsable 390 MB HTML rendering of the whole proof. This is autoformalization of the Wiles argument, not a new theorem, and it ran on an internal research model roughly comparable to Claude Fable 5.1 — but it demonstrates that machine-checked formalization of major mathematics is now achievable at agent scale.

quality.note: Official Anthropic research post with the open-source proof repository. Verification is kernel-based; semantic review of each intermediate theorem remains a human task, and the repo is labeled 'research artifact, not maintained.'

stories.title: Catch-up: IFM ships K2 Horizon, six fully open frontier models from 0.9B to 375B with data and recipe
stories.summary: MBZUAI's Institute of Foundation Models released K2 Horizon on September 3, a fleet of six open models (0.9B to 375B-A23B) that is unusual in shipping weights, code, training data and methodology under Apache 2.0, with day-zero vLLM/SGLang/Ollama support and FP8 variants. The 375B-A23B flagship is a sparse MoE with 23B active parameters and a native 512K context window; IFM claims the 0.9B/3.7B/7B sizes set state of the art in their classes and the 375B is competitive with closed frontier models on agentic work. The earlier edition missed this launch. Independent reproduction of the benchmark claims is still pending, but the openness of the training stack is the part builders can verify directly.

quality.note: Official IFM/MBZUAI press release and model repositories. Included as an explicitly labeled catch-up; only the release date is exposed on the page (noon UTC used). Benchmark claims are vendor-reported.

stories.title: Meta opens Muse Spark 1.3 max reasoning effort to all developers on Muse Code and the Model API
stories.summary: Meta released a new `reasoning_effort=max` tier for Muse Spark 1.3, the highest reasoning setting above xhigh, available on Muse Code and the Meta Model API with the base model (shipped September 2) unchanged. The model id stays `muse-spark-1.3` with a 1,048,576-token context and 131,072-token output limit; Meta says max delivers stronger coding and agentic performance than high/xhigh, and earlier third-party testing had the base 1.3 model at 62 on the Artificial Analysis index, behind only Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5. The tier is Standard-tier only (not Contributor tier), so it matters most for API cost/capability planning.

quality.note: Official Meta account announcing the tier (quoting CAIO Alexandr Wang); the base model release page is Meta's canonical page but dates from September 2. No separate model card for the max tier was linked from the post.

stories.title: xAI ships installable Grok Bot templates, led by a vendor-spend 'Haggle Bot'
stories.summary: xAI opened its Grok Bot template marketplace with 69 public bots, headlined by Haggle Bot, which maps vendor spend across Slack, Notion, Drive, Gmail, Hex and Ramp and found over $100K in savings in one internal SpaceXAI audit (e.g. $85,662/yr in unused SKUs). The release extends Grok Bot for Enterprise (launched September 3) from a managed agent into a templated agent ecosystem. The savings figures are a vendor-internal anecdote, and the enterprise CTA routes through a Cursor waitlist rather than a GA xAI enterprise SKU, so treat the marketplace as the launch and the numbers as directional.

quality.note: Official xAI product page and product-account launch post. Savings claims are one internal audit, not a third-party benchmark.

stories.title: Runway adds a self-serve Team Plan with pooled credits and agent connectors for 2-9 seats
stories.summary: Runway launched a Team Plan covering 2-9 seats with pooled credits, shared projects, commenting, agent skills and Agent Connectors. It is a distribution and collaboration move rather than a new model, but it puts enterprise-style governance (including the September 3 credit caps) into self-serve packaging. Pricing is on the public team page; adoption data is not yet available.

quality.note: Official Runway pricing page and X announcement. The pricing page is the only canonical URL linked in the post.

stories.title: SEC accelerates Nasdaq Texas rule change defining 'digital commodity' and opening 15% NAV buffer for active crypto trusts
stories.summary: The SEC granted accelerated approval (Release No. 34-106268, September 3) of a Nasdaq Texas amendment to Rule 5711(d) for Commodity-Based Trust Shares, which introduces an official 'digital commodity' definition, legalizes actively managed crypto strategies, and permits funds to hold up to 15% of NAV in instruments that initially fail strict listing criteria. The order explicitly cites a trust holding Bitcoin, Ether, Solana and XRP as digital commodities that currently meet the criteria. It is a generic-listing framework rather than a new fund approval, but it materially widens the shelf for multi-asset and actively managed crypto ETPs and extends the March 2026 joint SEC-CFTC commodity interpretation into exchange rules.

quality.note: Primary SEC order document (order dated September 3, 2026; date-only timestamp approximated to late ET) corroborated by two independent reports of the same release number and rule change.

stories.title: Coinbase files Form 1-N and BD-N to bring 24/7 single-stock perpetuals to US traders
stories.summary: Coinbase confirmed on September 3 that it filed SEC notice registrations (Form 1-N for Coinbase Derivatives and Form BD-N for Coinbase Financial Markets, both dated September 1) to bring single-stock perpetual futures onshore under the dual SEC-CFTC security-futures framework established by the 2000 CFMA. The company said it will work with both agencies, and the filings are deliberately routed through security futures rather than the CFTC-only self-certification path that CME Group is suing the CFTC over. This is a notice registration, not an approval: contract terms, leverage limits, clearing and a launch date are all still undisclosed.

quality.note: Official Coinbase post with copies of both filings reported; policy officer Shirzad confirmed the filings separately. Filings are notices, not approvals, and CME's lawsuit against the CFTC clouds the broader perps legal landscape.

stories.title: OCC grants preliminary conditional approval to OpenReserve Bank, a full-service national bank for tokenized deposits and digital assets
stories.summary: OCC Corporate Decision #1389 (September 2, 2026) grants preliminary conditional approval to charter OpenReserve Bank, N.A. in Salt Lake City as a full-service national bank — not a trust charter — with tokenized deposits, digital-asset custody and a planned stablecoin subsidiary issuing rUSD under the GENIUS Act. The conditions are strict: at least $210M paid-in capital, a 12% Tier 1 leverage ratio for three years, and Federal Reserve/FDIC approvals still outstanding. It is the clearest signal yet that regulators see blockchain-native companies fitting inside federal banking supervision rather than alongside it, and it is a16z-backed.

quality.note: Primary OCC decision letter (dated September 2, 2026; date-only timestamp used) corroborated by independent reporting and a CoinDesk post within the window. Preliminary only: final approval, FDIC insurance and Fed stock remain.

stories.title: South Korea publishes a three-phase roadmap to tokenize stocks, bonds and funds, ending in stablecoin settlement
stories.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission announced on September 4 a phased roadmap for tokenizing securities: phase 1 begins February 4, 2027 (when the Electronic Registration Act takes effect) with institutional money-market funds, bonds, unlisted stocks via trust and public fractional securities; phase 2 extends tokenization to all publicly offered securities; phase 3 builds on-chain payment infrastructure linked to stablecoins. Subordinate-statute revisions are due by end of September 2026. This is a government capital-markets infrastructure program — tokenized securities rather than Bitcoin — but it sets the template for regulated on-chain asset distribution that RWA projects are aiming for.

quality.note: Official FSC press release (meeting held September 4; date-only timestamp used, noon KST approximated to 04:00 UTC) corroborated by CoinDesk reporting of the same roadmap.

stories.title: National Sheriffs' Association shifts to neutral on the CLARITY Act ahead of the Senate cloture vote
stories.summary: The National Sheriffs' Association publicly moved from opposition to a neutral stance on the CLARITY Act on September 4, saying it wants to step back and let Congress build the regulatory framework — removing one of the highest-profile law-enforcement opponents ahead of the September 15 Senate cloture vote. Neutral is not support: the NSA's earlier letter argued Section 604 could exempt mixers and DeFi protocols from AML rules, and that letter's text remains paywalled. The shift matters mainly as a signal that the bill can clear the procedural hurdle without a formal law-enforcement block.

quality.note: Two independent outlets report the stance change; the NSA's own letter was not directly retrieved (Politico Pro is paywalled). Position statement, not new legislation.

stories.title: Hargreaves Lansdown lists nine Bitcoin and Ether ETNs, opening crypto to its ~2 million UK clients
stories.summary: The UK's largest retail wealth platform, Hargreaves Lansdown, listed nine BTC/ETH exchange-traded notes from iShares, CoinShares, WisdomTree, 21Shares, Invesco and Bitwise on September 4, following the FCA's October 2025 lift of the retail crypto-ETP ban. The products carry an appropriateness test and a 24-hour waiting period, and are not ISA-eligible after April 2026. It is a concrete retail distribution milestone in Europe's largest wealth-management market, but ETNs are note-based exposure, not spot BTC.

quality.note: Reported by two outlets from the platform's listing announcement; the BitcoinMagazine post had no link, so the CoinDesk piece serves as the canonical reporting URL.

stories.title: Trezor: ShipMonk shipping-provider breach extends to ~67,000 additional US customers
stories.summary: Trezor updated its incident disclosure on September 4 after its shipping provider ShipMonk told it that 2019-2021 US order data (~67,000 customers — names, emails, phones, shipping addresses, order numbers) was also in the earlier breach. Devices and keys were not compromised, but the exposed data is a phishing and physical-security risk for long-time holders. ShipMonk had previously attested that the old data was deleted, so this is a third-party logistics failure, not a Trezor firmware or key-derivation issue.

quality.note: Official Trezor blog update corroborated by CoinDesk reporting the same day. Scope is customer PII from order history, not device keys.

stories.title: iRobot unveils Roomba Duo, a main vacuum plus deployable companion robot that cleans under low furniture
stories.summary: At IFA 2026 in Berlin, iRobot unveiled the Roomba Duo, its first dual-unit system: a large robot that vacuums and steam-mops paired with an ultra-compact companion robot (8.3 cm tall) that a mechanical arm deploys from the main unit's dock to clean under beds, sofas and dining chairs. The pair share one home map and run from an autonomous mobile dock, and the current prototype uses the Roomba Plus 575 Combo as the deployable mini. It is still a prototype with no price or release date, but the 'Transformers of robot vacuums' architecture — specialized robots cooperating as one system — is a concrete design bet on multi-robot home autonomy.

quality.note: Official iRobot PR (September 4, 2026, 04:15 ET) with hands-on Tom's Guide coverage from the IFA floor. Prototype stage; no price or ship date disclosed.

stories.title: Catch-up: XPENG's robotics unit Dogotix raises over $900M at $6.3B valuation for the IRON humanoid
stories.summary: XPENG announced that its robotics business — spun off into a standalone subsidiary called Dogotix — signed share-purchase agreements raising more than US$900M at a post-money valuation above US$6.3B (~43 billion yuan), which the company calls the largest single-round private financing in China's embodied AI industry. The round was led by IDG Capital with Gaorong Ventures and strategic participation from Tencent and Alibaba, and funds Physical AI research, model training, data generation and mass-production facilities; the IRON humanoid (76 body DOF, 21 per hand, three in-house Turing chips at up to 2,250 TOPS) targets mass production by end of 2026 with external deliveries in 2027. The deal was announced August 24, outside the primary window, so it is included as a plainly labeled catch-up; it has not yet closed.

quality.note: Official XPENG announcement reported by multiple outlets; included as a labeled catch-up because the announcement predates the 30-hour window. Transaction is at the share-purchase-agreement stage and not closed.

stories.title: Minth and AGIBOT open Europe's first humanoid mass-production line in Serbia, targeting 20,000 units a year
stories.summary: Automotive Tier-1 supplier Minth and Shanghai's AGIBOT inaugurated serial humanoid and quadruped production at Minth's Šabac, Serbia site on September 2, with an initial €20M investment and a planned €200M Robotics Industrial Park in Inđija targeting up to 20,000 units annually. Phase-1 targets are roughly 5,000 assembled units, and Serbian President Vučić attended the opening. Units will run AGIBOT's 'One Robotic Body, Three Intelligences' architecture, and the in-country build is aimed at continuous physical-interaction data for training embodied models. It is a concrete outside-China manufacturing bet, but ramping a line in a new automotive complex will test supply chain and quality control at scale.

quality.note: Dedicated robotics industry coverage of the inauguration (Wednesday, September 2, 2026; date-only timestamp used). The launch itself is documented with state officials present, but the AGIBOT/Minth press pages were not independently retrieved in this window.

stories.title: IFA 2026 opens in Berlin with a concentrated Chinese embodied-AI push: Galbot's autonomous G1 store, XGSynBot's Z1, and a humanoid 'runway'
stories.summary: IFA 2026 (September 4-8, Messe Berlin) opened with Hall 25's IFA Next zone dominated by Chinese embodied-AI companies: Galbot (China's highest-valued unlisted humanoid firm) is running its G1 in a fully autonomous pharmacy/store demo, and its ET1 biped — which played autonomous tennis against a former pro last month — remains an R&D platform with no pricing. XGSynBot debuted its Z1 wheeled humanoid, claiming a six-second end-effector tool swap that no independent engineer has yet verified, and on September 5 a 'Robots on the Runway' event will walk humanoids from AGIBOT, Unitree and EngineAI down a catwalk. The context is the FCC's July 28 Covered List action barring new Chinese robots from US authorization, which makes IFA the de facto European launchpad for the sector this year.

quality.note: On-floor industry reporting of multiple simultaneous debuts; performance claims (especially XGSynBot's 6-second swap) are company-claimed and not independently verified. An event report, not a single product launch.

stories.title: CJ Logistics deploys dual-arm humanoid robots in a live South Korean warehouse for the first time
stories.summary: CJ Logistics placed two humanoid dual-arm robots at its Olive Young distribution center in Yongin, the first live logistics use of humanoids in South Korea, where they insert cushioning material on packaging lines and will expand to picking, sorting and inspection. The robots run on a Robot Foundation Model (RFM) built with Robotis (hardware), Aidin Robotics (hands) and Realworld AI (model), and live operational data feeds back into RFM training. It is a narrow single-task deployment rather than unsupervised autonomy, but it is real commercial floor time — the kind of evidence the sector has been short of.

quality.note: Sector news report (September 4, 2026; date-only timestamp used) of a live deployment. Current scope is one task (cushion insertion); expansion plans are stated, not yet executed.

stories.title: Catch-up: ORAI calcium channels and STIM1 in capillaries are essential for matching blood flow to brain activity
stories.summary: A Science Signaling paper (issue of September 1, 2026) shows that ORAI1/ORAI3 calcium channels and their regulator STIM1 in capillary endothelial cells are required for capillaries to signal upstream arterioles to dilate during prolonged neuronal activity; endothelial-specific knockout of Stim1 or Orai1 disrupted that signaling, impaired sustained arteriole dilation and reduced evoked blood flow in mouse somatosensory cortex. Mice with the deficiency showed cognitive impairment (Stim1/Orai1) or anxiety-like behavior (Orai3), linking impaired capillary-to-arteriole signaling to early vascular-dementia-like phenotypes. This is mouse physiology, not a human intervention, but it identifies a druggable endothelial mechanism sitting at the intersection of cerebrovascular health and cognitive aging.

quality.note: Peer-reviewed paper in the current Science Signaling issue (accepted August 13, 2026; issue dated September 1, 2026, with the journal's X post in-window on September 5). Labeled catch-up because the issue date predates the primary window. Mouse study; no human data.

stories.title: Science Immunology: platelet-derived serotonin drives age-related lung clotting and severe respiratory disease after SARS-CoV-2
stories.summary: A Science Immunology paper shows that platelets from older mice release more serotonin when activated, and that platelet-released serotonin drives platelet aggregation and fibrin deposition in the lung microvasculature after SARS-CoV-2 infection, producing severe respiratory dysfunction; blocking serotonin signaling reduced disease severity in the aging-mouse model. Middle-aged mice and aged human healthy donors both showed enhanced platelet serotonin release, tying the mechanism to human aging as well. It is an animal study with supporting human-donor observations, not a treatment — but it points at a druggable, age-dependent clotting pathway relevant to severe-age-90s respiratory outcomes and vascular aging generally.

quality.note: Peer-reviewed paper flagged by the journal's official account in-window. Primary evidence is in aging mice; human contribution is limited to donor platelet observations. No medical advice: a mechanism study, not an intervention trial.

stories.title: Nature: US military plan to redirect hundreds of millions in NIH infectious-disease research to DoD biodefense
stories.summary: Nature reports that the NIH and the Department of Defense have signed a 10-year agreement under which hundreds of millions of dollars in NIAID infectious-disease projects will shift to military biodefence programmes ('Operation Prevailing Edge'), with the full agreement targeted for end of this fiscal year. NIH director Jay Bhattacharya defends the arrangement as a partnership, while biosecurity researchers warn that moving work away from NIAID fragments pandemic preparedness and changes the transparency and clinical-translation norms that define NIH-funded science. For biotech and longevity programs, it is a reminder that federal research money now has a second, less transparent destination, and that grant-portfolio strategy may matter more than ever.

quality.note: Nature news piece (based on two NIH employees; the full agreement is not yet public) and the journal's official X post. A funding/infrastructure shift, not a scientific result.

stories.title: FDA raises the bar for inspecting foreign clinical-trial sites as China-based trials surge
stories.summary: The FDA's official account announced on September 4 that it is expanding inspections of foreign clinical-trial sites, adding resources and increasing scrutiny of data from sites it cannot access, as China-based trial activity surges. The scope and effective date were not detailed in the post, which links BioSpace's reporting rather than an FDA.gov release. For longevity and biotech programs, the practical effect is that any trial with significant China or other ex-US sites will face tighter inspection, data-access and site-qualification requirements — a direct cost and schedule factor in multi-site aging trials.

quality.note: Official FDA account post; the linked BioSpace piece (not FDA.gov) carries the detail. Scope and effective date not in the post.
